newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt member criticises flight plans.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt member criticises flight plans.

text.p: Australian government member Andrew Thomson on Wednesday criticised plans released by Transport Minister John Sharp for new flight paths from Sydney Airport.

Thomson, parliamentary secretary to Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer, said the new flight paths over the eastern suburbs of Sydney were unfair and contradicted Sharp's own directive to AirServices Australia.
"Last March, Mr Sharp clearly laid down in his ministerial direction that noise is to be maximised over water and non-residential areas," Thomson said in a statement.
"The bureaucrats have totally ignored this instruction."
Under the plans, a new jet flight path would be created over people living in the suburbs of North Randwick, Queens Park and Bondi Junction.
"While the overall plan has many sensible aspects to it, the proposed new jet flight path is obviously unacceptable and must be changed," he said.
"I will fight long and hard until this is achieved."
Sharp said earlier on Wednesday he was considering the new flight paths, which were released in conjunction with a report showing that airline traffic moving through Sydney would double in 13 years.
Sharp said the report showed there was a need for a second major airport in Sydney, rather than the small overflow operation that was previously planned.
